_comment: THE MANAGER'S CHECKLIST. Every work item in the CURRENT manager session's
scope, and the state of each.
OPERATOR DIRECTIVE, 2026-09-01, verbatim in intent: 'every manager session
keeps a detailed checklist of work items in its scope (this may be updated
as work progresses and the workplan is adapted, eg an unforeseen blocker
that needs to be resolved to release the rest of the items) - and every
status update should start with the checklist, then summary of what has
been done (recently) and what's next.'
SO THE REPORTING CONTRACT IS FIXED: checklist -> recently done -> next.
In that order, every time. A status update that opens with a narrative is
not following this.
WHY IT LIVES IN THE REPO AND NOT IN A SESSION'S CONTEXT. Same reason as
MANAGER-LEASE.json and SESSIONS.json: it must survive its holder's DEATH
and be readable by a manager arriving COLD. A checklist held only in
context is lost exactly when a successor most needs it, and re-deriving it
costs the successor the hours that produced it.
IT IS ADAPTIVE, NOT A FROZEN PLAN. The directive is explicit that it
changes as work progresses -- an unforeseen blocker that must be resolved
to release the rest is a first-class edit, not a failure of planning. Add
the blocker as its own item, point the blocked items at it, and say so.
STATES ARE NEVER COLLAPSED. 'delegated' is not 'in progress' and neither is
'done'; 'blocked' names WHAT it waits on. Most importantly 'done' means
MERGED AND OBSERVED, while 'landed_unproven' means the code is in and its
effect has NOT been seen on the fleet -- the distinction this whole system
keeps paying for when it is skipped.
THE MANAGER DOES NOT EXECUTE THESE ITEMS. Operator-directed the same day:
'the manager session only manages and does not take even small items,
because that means they're not focused on what they're actually supposed
to be doing.' An item with owner 'manager' is a MANAGEMENT act (a merge, a
deploy, a lease heartbeat, a spawn), never a build.

Surfaced by session_01LvzsinECH8HP in #10687 and then MEASURED INDEPENDENTLY BY THE MANAGER rather than taken on report — plain curl, no Authorization header, from outside the VM against https://ict-bot.duckdns.org : /api/bot/db/table/trades -> HTTP 200, total 5,318 · order_packages -> 200, 4,275 · balance_snapshots -> 200, 29,892. NEGATIVE CONTROL: device_tokens -> HTTP 404, so #10682's exclusion genuinely holds and the probe can distinguish a refusal from a serve. The filing session counted `signals` at 2,301,022 rows. === WHY IT HAPPENED, AND IT IS NOT A CODING ERROR: CLAUDE.md justifies the Data Explorer as Tier-1 on the premise 'no secrets in either DB' — a claim about CREDENTIALS, not about the CONFIDENTIALITY of the trading record. That judgement was made while the API sat on a firewalled IP reachable only server-side by Streamlit. Caddy was then added (2026-08-13) so the browser-direct Svelte SPA could reach the API over HTTPS, and NOBODY RE-DERIVED THE TIER DECISION AFTER THE TRANSPORT CHANGED. The route did not become less safe; the world became able to reach it. === HONEST SEVERITY, in the direction that does not overstate: this is a CONFIDENTIALITY exposure, NOT a control path. The explorer is SELECT-only on a mode=ro connection with bound values and schema-validated identifiers; nothing writes, no order can be placed, and no credential is reachable now that device_tokens is excluded. Nobody's money can be moved with it. What is exposed is the operator's complete trading record — every trade, order package and balance snapshot. === ⚠️ DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED TONIGHT, and that is a decision rather than an omission. Gating a live public read route is Tier-2, and the Data Explorer tab of the Svelte SPA reaches this route BROWSER-DIRECT, so adding a bearer would break a working operator surface. Doing that unannounced at 02:00 while the operator sleeps trades a three-week-old read exposure for a broken dashboard they wake up to. The options worth putting to them: leave it (the record is not secret), gate it behind DASHBOARD_API_TOKEN and teach the SPA to send one, or put Caddy basic-auth in front of /api/bot/db/* only. === ⚠️ THE BLAST RADIUS IS NOW BOUNDED BY MEASUREMENT, NOT BY REASONING — the manager probed the same public host unauthenticated for anything WRITEABLE or PRIVILEGED and every gate refused: POST /api/bot/prop/report (the one route that writes the journal) -> HTTP 401 'missing authorization', confirming its documented FAIL-CLOSED behaviour; GET /api/pnl -> 401 and GET /api/status -> 401, so require_session is genuinely enforced on both session-gated routes; GET /api/diag/version -> 401 without a bearer. SO: NO UNAUTHENTICATED WRITE EXISTS ANYWHERE on the public surface, and no privileged read. The exposure is exactly and only the Tier-1 READ surface. That is what makes 'confidentiality, not control' a measured statement rather than a hedge, and it is why this can wait for the operator rather than being fixed unilaterally overnight. === Incidental confirmation worth keeping: this independently verifies CLAUDE.md's 2026-08-13 correction that require_session enforcement IS live on /api/pnl and /api/status — an earlier version of that row said 'issuance only', which was stale in the dangerous direction. Field now matches comment.

So a low fill rate on these legs is not lost opportunity — it is a second leg correctly denied a symbol another leg already owns. === THE SHARPEST CASE, filed as PB-20260902-MGC-TREND-1H-IS-LIVE-AND-STRUCTURALLY-CANNOT-TRADE: `mgc_trend_1h` is execution:live and enabled:true with 95 decisions, ZERO fills, ZERO closed trades since 2026-07-26. 55 of 55 of its suppressions were raised while MGC was already open on ib_paper, held ALWAYS by a sibling (ict_scalp_mgc_15m 48, mgc_pullback_1d 7) and NEVER by itself, because it has never held a position. items.title: A sub-session's 'I'll stay available' is a hand-off nothing can act on
items.note: MEASURED TWICE TONIGHT, and the second time it cost a real hand-off. The merge-train sub-session (session_01CKcZFm) ended its turn IDLE at 01:46:45Z with post_turn_summary 'staying available to re-resolve as manager merges' — an explicit offer to be re-invoked. When two of its PRs needed exactly that re-resolve, the manager tried `SendMessage` to it and got: **'No agent named session_01CKcZFm... is reachable. Use ListAgents to see everyone you can message.'** `ListAgents` lists only in-process agents and local sessions; a CCR cloud sub-session appears in NEITHER direction. === SO 'STAYING AVAILABLE' IS A DEAD END THAT READS AS A HAND-OFF. That session was holding full context on two conflicted PRs — which files, which resolution rule, what it had already tried — and NONE of it was reachable. The manager had to spawn a fresh session (session_015oCrkh) and re-supply everything it already knew. It worked, but the duplicated context is the cost, and the operator has said that cost is acceptable — which is not the same as it being invisible. === ⚠️ THIS IS THE COORDINATION LIMIT THE OPERATING-MODEL DESIGN ALREADY NAMES, observed live: 'a session that dies cannot run its own close-out', so state must be written to the WORK OBJECT as work happens rather than held in a session that expects to be woken. An IDLE session is the same case as a dead one for this purpose — the design's three mechanisms (incremental progress, a lease per session, a reaper) are the answer, and none of them is 'message it again'. === TWO THINGS A FUTURE MANAGER SHOULD DO DIFFERENTLY: (1) never write a spawn prompt that invites a session to idle and await follow-up — tell it to finish, write its state down, and stop; (2) do not read `post_turn_summary: staying available` as an owner. It is not one. The row is `queued` rather than filed to a backlog because the fix is a change to how sessions are SPAWNED and how hand-off state is RECORDED, which is operating-model work, not a bug in a file. === RE-TESTED 2026-09-02T04:15Z AND IT HOLDS, with a sharper statement. Every running sub-session's CCR record advertises `cross_session_inbound: "available"`, which reads as a capability. ListAgents from this manager returns 'No reachable agents — no other Claude session is running on this machine right now'. So the field describes a CCR-side inbound path, not this session's peer graph, and a manager reading it would conclude it can message a sub-session when it cannot. That is the same unprovenanced-output shape MI-27 and MI-36 are about, one layer up in the tooling. Practical consequence, hit tonight: #10739 needed a fix, its author was ALIVE and self-reported review_ready, and I could not tell it — I had to post a PR comment and hope it reads it.
items.correction: 2026-09-02: MI-32'S CONCLUSION WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE. It recorded that an idle cloud sub-session is unreachable, and that was true of the mechanisms it TESTED (SendMessage / ListAgents, which do not enumerate or address cloud sessions from this manager). It generalised from those two to 'unreachable', and that generalisation cost a full archive-and-respawn cycle on MI-37 and nearly cost another here. A SESSION-BOUND ROUTINE IS A WORKING CHANNEL. create_trigger with persistent_session_id (no cron, no run_once_at -- a poke-only Routine) followed by fire_trigger delivers a prompt into a specific existing session. MEASURED 2026-09-02T05:35Z on session_01PcirVtpMXJGiKm2548nkrR (the MI-39 fix session, which had gone idle mid-task without pushing): immediately before the fire it read session_status=SESSION_STATUS_IDLE / connection_status=disconnected; immediately after, SESSION_STATUS_RUNNING / connected, same session id, context intact. Trigger trig_01NcP7PmwUeFPCbRN4G61VQX. ⚠️ ONE REAL LIMIT, DO NOT OMIT IT WHEN USING THIS: the tool warns that a Routine created this way stores no MCP connectors, so THE FIRED TURN RUNS WITHOUT mcp__* TOOLS. A poked session keeps Bash/git/file tools and therefore keeps the pr-opener and board-post relays, but loses mcp__github__* outright. That is fine for a sub-session that already 403s on GitHub writes and works through the relays; it is NOT fine for one that needs the GitHub MCP to finish. ⚠️ AND THIS IS NOT A REPLY CHANNEL: the poked session cannot answer back. It is a one-way wake, so the manager still learns the outcome from the branch, the PR, or get_session -- never from a message. THE MANAGER LESSON: an idle sub-session is a RESUMABLE session, not a dead one. Poke it before archiving; a respawn duplicates context and loses whatever the idle session already worked out.

items.title: The merge-ordering protocol, learned by getting it wrong three times in one night
items.note: Written into #10728 and then PROVEN under live test the same hour. The rule: resolve one → merge it → resolve the next against the NEW main. Batch-resolve-then-batch-merge cannot converge, because each merge invalidates every sibling resolve not yet landed — measured cost tonight was two wasted resolves on #10679. Under the protocol, four PRs merged in sequence with zero re-conflicts. TWO refinements learned in the doing and worth keeping: (1) a manager-only PR is the standing EXCEPTION — its conflict surface is empty, so it merges at any point in the queue without disturbing an in-flight sibling (#10728 merged while #10679 was open and #10679 stayed clean). items.title: A manager spawns its own handoff manager, which pings the operator that it has taken over, with a link to itself
items.operator_ask: Operator, 2026-09-02: 'the possibility of the manager spawning its own handoff manager session at its own discretion - this requires that we be certain about continuity robustness, and the new session needs to send a ping that it has taken over with a link to itself.'
verified_today: SELF-IDENTIFICATION WORKS. get_session with session_id OMITTED returns the CALLING session's own record, id included (verified 2026-09-02T06:21Z from this manager: returned session_011JWFxuYAaEQKCFCmG6gnHJ). So a successor can build https://claude.ai/code/<its own id> without being told what it is -- which the spawning manager CANNOT pass in the prompt anyway, since the id does not exist until create_session returns.

THE PING CAN CARRY THE LINK TODAY. Read on main 2026-09-02: notify_on_pull._render_ping_message emits `title`, `summary` and `chat_url` from its recognised-key list. A takeover ping using those keys renders with its link. ⚠️ BUT `message` IS NOT IN THAT LIST -- a ping built with it renders as a BARE EVENT LABEL, which is exactly the empty 03:24 digest the operator screenshotted. The takeover ping MUST use recognised keys, or it announces nothing.
SPAWNING WORKS: 11 sub-sessions created this session via create_session with explicit source_url + source_revision.

THE LEASE ALREADY HAS THE HANDOVER PRIMITIVES: manager_lease.py has release + claim, and CLAIMABLE = {expired, released, absent}. A HELD lease REFUSES a claim, so the successor cannot simply take it -- the outgoing manager must release first, or the successor must --force with a reason.
proposed_protocol: 1. Outgoing SPAWNS the successor (create_session, explicit source_url+revision) and REGISTERS it in SESSIONS.json in the same action.
2. Outgoing RELEASES the lease and PUSHES it. An unpushed release protects nothing -- the successor reads origin.
3. Successor CLAIMS the lease, pushes, and PINGS with `title`+`summary`+`chat_url` naming itself.

4. ⚠️ OUTGOING DOES NOT EXIT YET. It polls the LEASE FROM ORIGIN -- the lease is the only shared state both sides can see, and there is NO back-channel (a woken session cannot reply; cross-session inbound does not reach back). When holder == successor, the handover is CONFIRMED and the outgoing stands down.

5. If nobody has claimed within a bounded window, the outgoing RE-CLAIMS (released is claimable by anyone, including the original) and reports a FAILED handoff. This step is the robustness the operator asked for: the outgoing must not disappear on the ASSUMPTION its successor is alive.
risks_named: ⚠️ THE GAP WINDOW IS THE REAL HAZARD. Between release and claim, NOBODY holds the lease while sub-sessions keep running -- the lease's own doc is explicit that sub-sessions do not depend on it and what pauses is SUPERVISION. If the successor dies at spawn (which happened TWICE tonight on MI-37, both times on repo provisioning), the system is left with running sub-sessions, no manager, and nobody aware. Step 5 exists for exactly this and is the part that must be proven, not assumed.

⚠️ A SUCCESSOR THAT CLAIMS AND THEN DIES IS WORSE THAN ONE THAT NEVER CLAIMED: the lease reads `held` for its full 90-minute TTL, so the time-based takeover that protects against death is precisely what delays discovery.

⚠️ CONTINUITY IS NOT PROVEN UNTIL MI-43 LANDS. 'Certain about continuity robustness' is the operator's own precondition, and today both handoff records (SESSIONS.json, OPEN-PRS.json) are maintained by REMEMBERING -- the mechanism that failed twice tonight at 3-of-6 and 6-of-9.

COST, as an independent argument FOR bounded manager sessions: this manager session has cost $885.84 with 1.31 BILLION cache-read tokens (read from its own get_session record, 2026-09-02T06:21Z). A manager that never hands over accumulates this indefinitely.

blocked_on.note: Still ordered behind MI-43 -- the readiness check should gate the handoff it is being tested with. If MI-43 is not landed when the handoff is due, run the handoff anyway and record WHICH criteria went unverified rather than claiming a clean pass.

items.operator_decision: 2026-09-02: THIS HANDOFF IS THE ACCEPTANCE TEST. Operator: 'we'll obviously test it on this handoff, so we can verify before closing here.' So MI-44 is no longer a deferred design -- it is exercised at THIS session's close, and the outgoing manager stays alive to observe it. That is the only way the protocol gets proven rather than asserted, and it matches the repo's own standard that a deploy is not an observation.
acceptance_criteria: 1. The successor CLAIMS the lease: docs/claude/work/MANAGER-LEASE.json on ORIGIN reads state=held with holder=<successor id>. Read from origin, never from a local tree.

2. The operator RECEIVES a takeover ping that RENDERS -- carrying a link to the successor. ⚠️ A ping that arrives as a bare event label is a FAILURE of this criterion, not a partial pass: that is the exact defect #10747 exists to fix, and `message` is not a recognised renderer key.

3. The successor demonstrates it can READ the handoff state it inherited -- naming the live sub-sessions from SESSIONS.json and the open PRs with their CONDITIONS from OPEN-PRS.json. ⚠️ Inheriting the files is not the test; USING them is. A successor that claims the lease and cannot say what #10746's staging condition is has failed, because that is the case where a half-informed manager is more dangerous than an ignorant one.
4. Only after 1-3 are OBSERVED does the outgoing manager stand down. If any fails, it RE-CLAIMS and reports the failed handoff rather than leaving the system unmanaged.

items.title: stop-hook-git-check pressures the manager to commit a running sub-agent's in-flight source changes
items.observed: 2026-09-02, FOUR times in ~20 minutes. `~/.claude/stop-hook-git-check.sh` fires 'There are uncommitted changes ... Please commit and push' whenever the working tree is dirty. It has no notion of WHOSE changes those are. Every firing today was on a live sub-agent's work, not mine — my branch was in sync with origin each time.
items.what_complying_would_have_done: ⚠️ NOT a tidiness issue. The dirty paths were config/instruments.yaml, src/units/accounts/execute.py, src/units/accounts/qty_legalize.py, precision.py, instrument_profile.py, profile_loader.py and two test files — a live, unreviewed, ORDER-PATH-ADJACENT change. Committing them would have (a) put unreviewed order-path code into a PR about recording operator decisions, and (b) taken the work out from under a running agent that had not finished or tested it.
items.root_cause: One git working tree, two writers. The hook assumes a single writer per checkout. It is correct for that case and actively harmful for this one. The manager's own `git checkout` compounds it: it does not move an agent's uncommitted files aside, it DRAGS them onto whatever branch the manager lands on.
what_actually_prevents_it: Sub-sessions in their OWN CONTAINER (create_session) rather than in-process agents — used for MI-53 today, and the reason it was used.

Agent worktree isolation — ATTEMPTED today and REFUSED: 'Cannot create agent worktree: not in a git repository', because the session cwd is /home/user while the repo is /home/user/Metis-Insights. Spawning with the repo as cwd would likely fix it; UNVERIFIED, do not assert it.
NEVER `git add -A` while any agent shares the tree. Explicit paths only. This is the discipline that saved it today after the first near-miss.
items.the_honest_residual: ⚠️ The hook is not wrong to fire — it cannot know. So this is not 'fix the hook to be quiet'; a hook that learned to ignore dirty trees would stop catching the case it exists for. The fix is on the SPAWN side: agents should not share a tree. Recorded so the next manager does not resolve four hook warnings by committing someone else's work.

items.title: The open-PR handoff record can never read clean, because the PR that maintains it is itself an open PR
items.observed: handoff_check's open_prs check FAILS in both directions by construction. Every open PR must have a row (recorded - observed_open -> stale_row; observed_open - recorded -> unrecorded). The PR that maintains the rows is itself an open PR, so it needs a row, and merging it makes that row stale. MEASURED LIVE 2026-09-02: #10775 merged (d08cac48) about NINETY SECONDS after a branch recorded a row for it -- the row was correct when written and stale before the PR carrying it could open. The manager then pruned it and opened #10777, whose own row went stale on merge (cd8554fa). Two full iterations of the loop, observed, not argued.
items.what_complying_would_have_done: Nothing. There is no compliant sequence: the gate cannot read `ready` on the merge that closes it. Restating the regress in each PR body -- which is what happened twice -- documents the trap without removing it, and the operator correctly named that as the failure: a structural fix was needed, not a better description.
items.root_cause: TWO, and only the second is the terminator. (1) TWO POPULATIONS CONFLATED UNDER ONE KEY: open_prs[] holds both an in-flight CLAIM (this PR is open, here is its owner and blocker) and the durable DECISION RECORD (what the operator actually said, verbatim). Only the first should be graded against the live open list; the second is HISTORY and is MORE load-bearing after the merge than before -- #10746's conditional Tier-2 approval (bybit_1 demo only, real-money bybit_2 accepted as exposed) is precisely what a successor must not lose. So 'pruning a stale row' DELETES decision knowledge in order to satisfy a freshness rule: the same shape as the OPEN-ITEMS cap that instructed a session to EVICT a valid row, which CLAUDE.md already records as a failure. (2) A COMMIT CANNOT RECORD ITS OWN MERGE. Whatever writes a row's terminal state must run OUTSIDE the commit being merged, and nothing did.
items.what_actually_prevents_it: Four parts, spawned as MI-57. (A) SPLIT THE FILE: open_prs[] graded against live, settled_prs[] never compared -- pruning becomes a MOVE, so knowledge is preserved and the freshness check keeps its teeth. (B) A POST-MERGE RECONCILER on push:main that moves a row whose PR is no longer open into settled_prs[] stamped with terminal/merge_sha/observed_at. Running outside the merging commit is what terminates the regress. (C) grade_completeness reads only open_prs[]; a NEW finding fails a settled_prs[] row with terminal=closed_unmerged and no disposition, because an abandoned PR with no stated reason IS real lost knowledge. (D) A DEAD RECONCILER MUST BE VISIBLE: if a stale row exists AND last_reconciled_sha != current main sha, the message says the RECONCILER has not run -- a different finding from a session forgetting, never collapsed into stale_row. (E) MEASURED CONSTRAINT ON (B), recorded here AND relayed. ⚠️ THIS ROW SAID 'a manager CANNOT message a running sub-session' AND THAT WAS WRONG -- do not re-quote it. The true statement is narrower: SendMessage/ListAgents do not ADDRESS cloud sessions from a manager container (measured -- SendMessage to the session id returned 'No agent named ... is reachable'), and the manager generalised from those two tools to the capability. A session-bound Routine DOES reach it: create_trigger with persistent_session_id set and BOTH cron_expression and run_once_at omitted, then fire_trigger. Two limits travel with it -- the fired turn runs WITHOUT mcp__* tools (so never tell it to pull a job log; quote the log INTO the prompt), and it is ONE-WAY, so the outcome is read from the branch/PR/get_session and never as a reply. The constraint below is therefore BOTH a relayed instruction and a review criterion on the draft PR: `main` is branch-protected and a direct push is REJECTED -- I tried one for this very commit and got `GH006 ... 3 of 3 required status checks are expected`. The repo already solved this: `.github/actions/commit-to-main` lands a change via a PAT-authored auto-merge PR with `verify-merged: true`, whose own comment records BL-20260706-GPU-BURST-LEDGER-PUSH-RACE (a direct push rejected, rows SILENTLY dropped, the $10 spend gate defeated). ⚠️ THAT CREATES THE REGRESS FROM THE OTHER SIDE: the reconciler's own landing PR is an open PR and would itself need a row. The resolution is a TYPED exclusion -- bot author AND `automation/` head-branch prefix, BOTH, never either -- which is categorically different from the rejected exemption: an automation landing PR carries no owner session, no intent and no operator decision, i.e. none of the three things this record exists to carry, so its absence cannot hide a forgotten human decision. A bare 'skip bots' is WRONG and must fail a test: a Claude-opened PR is bot-authored in the API sense and must still require a row.
items.the_honest_residual: The fix depends on a workflow actually firing, and this repo has a documented history of machinery that looks armed and is not -- probes.yml and due-list.yml at zero scheduled runs, two Claude Routines enabled:true with next_run_at 0001-01-01. That is exactly why (D) exists: the failure mode is not 'the reconciler is wrong' but 'the reconciler silently stopped and stale rows read as a session's negligence'. items.title: Work-decision prompts are answerable only on the trader bot, because nothing polls the dedicated Claude bot
items.tier: 2 (a live service gains a polling loop; no order path)
items.observed: Operator direction 2026-09-02, on seeing the first live prompt: 'that's supposed to be showing up in Cloudbot. Right? Not on the trader one, the decisions.' Correct. #10778 (merged 133587f1) routes prompts to the TRADER bot via telegram_decisions.answerable_route(), deliberately NOT claude_route(). Measured in that PR: the trader token is polled by ict-telegram-bot.service with a CallbackQueryHandler; the prop token is polled by ict-claude-bridge.service despite its name; TELEGRAM_CLAUDE_BOT_SECRET is polled by NOTHING. The operator DOES receive pings on ClaudeBot (an OPS deploy ping landed there at 10:11Z and they screenshotted it), which is exactly the distinction: sending needs only a token, a BUTTON needs a polling process to collect the callback_query.
items.what_complying_would_have_done: Nothing was violated. The build's choice was correct given what exists -- pointing prompts at ClaudeBot today would have shipped DEAD BUTTONS THAT LOOK HEALTHY, which is strictly worse than the wrong-channel state, and the PR said so explicitly rather than picking claude_route() because the name matched. The gap is that only half the capability exists, not that the wrong half was built.
items.root_cause: DELIVERY AND ANSWERABILITY ARE DIFFERENT PROPERTIES and only the first was ever built for the Claude bot. OI-20260901-CLAUDE-CHANNEL-SEPARATION-SHIPPED-BUT-UNPROVEN tracks the delivery half; nothing tracked the second, because until a button existed nobody needed the Claude bot to be polled. A channel that can be written to but not answered on reads as a working two-way channel from the operator's side right up until the first tap.
items.what_actually_prevents_it: MI-58 builds BOTH halves in one PR, in order: (1) make the Claude bot genuinely polled with a CallbackQueryHandler wired to the SAME handle_decision_callback -- not a fork, one owner, so the route stays the single owner of every refusal; (2) only THEN point answerable_route() at it. Plus the state that makes a regression visible: a startup line naming which token is polled and whether a handler is attached, and a sweep HOLD with a WARNING when the answerable bot is not confirmed polled -- three states, never collapsed (polled_with_handler / token_only_not_polled / unknown), because 'the button rendered' and 'the button works' are otherwise indistinguishable from the operator's side.
items.the_honest_residual: A green harness cannot prove this: the done-condition is a real tap on ClaudeBot producing a work_decision_transit.jsonl row, which needs the operator. The trader-bot round-trip IS already proven end to end (2026-09-02T10:16:36Z, chosen=accept_ungated, submitted_by=telegram), so MI-58 changes WHERE it happens and must not be read as re-proving WHETHER it works. And if the VM's .env lacks TELEGRAM_CLAUDE_BOT_SECRET the build stops at a manager/operator action -- it must NOT be worked around, and must NOT reuse TELEGRAM_CLAUDE_BOT_TOKEN, which drives the PROP bot.

items.title: /status and /decisions — pull the status update and every waiting decision on demand, instead of only receiving them as they fire
items.tier: 2 (a live service gains command handlers; no order path)
items.observed: Operator ask 2026-09-02, immediately after the first decision round-trip closed: a /status command returning the status update 'with the checklist and everything', and a /decisions command so every still-unanswered decision 'can all pop up at once, in case I don't get them as they come in'. The second names a real gap the push channel cannot close by itself: a prompt that fires while the operator is away is not re-offered, and the periodic sweep deliberately asks ONCE per request (a per-process re-ask is BL-20260823-TARGET-NAKED-COOLDOWN-RESETS-ON-EVERY-RESTART, which put 202 CRITICALs on the operator's channel). PULL is the correct complement to PUSH here, not a duplicate of it.
items.what_complying_would_have_done: Nothing was violated; this is new capability. Worth recording is the SEQUENCING constraint the ask does not mention: a /command reaches only a bot some process is POLLING, exactly like a button, so on ClaudeBot these arrive WITH MI-58 and not before it. Building them against a hardcoded token would have created a second migration the moment MI-58 lands.
items.root_cause: n/a — a feature request. The dependency is structural: DELIVERY needs only a token, but a COMMAND and a BUTTON both need a polling process. MI-58 is what makes ClaudeBot satisfy that; MI-59 must not duplicate the decision.
items.what_actually_prevents_it: Both commands register on telegram_decisions.answerable_route() -- the SAME resolver the prompts use -- so they work today on whatever bot is genuinely polled and follow MI-58 to ClaudeBot automatically, with no second migration and no operator decision required. /decisions reuses the sweep's own prompt/keyboard builder rather than a second copy, because two copies of the callback_data construction is how the 64-byte budget and the key-digest scheme drift apart. /status prints in the operator's required order (checklist -> recently done -> next) and STAMPS the sha it read plus whether the VM tree is behind main, three states never collapsed (synced / behind_main / unknown) -- measured today, the decisions route read `in_transit` for minutes after the answer was already committed to main, purely because the VM had not synced, so a confident status over a stale tree is a live failure mode and not a hypothetical. A truncated checklist must state how many items it omitted; a /decisions with nothing waiting must say so explicitly, because silence is indistinguishable from a broken command.
items.the_honest_residual: A green harness proves none of it: the done-condition is the operator typing each command and getting a correct reply, which needs them. Authorization is the sharper risk -- the repo is PUBLIC and the bot username is discoverable, so both commands expose internal state to anyone who finds the bot unless they answer only the operator's own chat; the spec requires reusing the existing handlers' auth notion rather than inventing a second one, and that is the thing to check hardest at review. And /status reads the MANAGER's checklist, which is only as honest as the manager keeping it -- a stale as_of will render as confidently as a fresh one, which the sha stamp mitigates but does not solve.

items.title: The decision round-trip ends in the repo and stops — the session that asked learns the answer only by polling
items.tier: 1 for the investigation; the build depends on what it touches. No order path either way.
items.observed: Operator ask on watching the first round-trip close: 'can we add a push on the end of that so that when the answer gets to the repo, it knows to push it to the session instead of waiting for the session to pull'. MEASURED against the machinery that shipped today: a decision request carries object_id, request_id, options, urgency and context -- and NOTHING identifying the session that asked. So there is currently no address to push to, whatever the transport turns out to be.
items.what_complying_would_have_done: n/a -- a feature request, and a well-aimed one. Phase H's own design says visibility is the enforcement mechanism this system has never had; a channel that carries a question outward and cannot carry the answer back to the asker is half of that.
items.root_cause: The round-trip was designed to make truth land in the REPO, which it does correctly. Delivery back to the ASKER was never in scope, so the asking session's identity was never recorded. That is a gap in the object schema before it is a gap in transport.
items.what_actually_prevents_it: MI-60, and its FIRST deliverable is deliberately not code: a feasibility doc stating per claim what was TESTED versus READ FROM DOCUMENTATION. ⚠️ The manager made exactly this error today -- declared 'a manager cannot message a running sub-session' off ONE failed SendMessage, wrote it into a merged PR body and a checklist row, and it was FALSE. A session-bound Routine (create_trigger with persistent_session_id, no cron, no run_once_at, then fire_trigger) IS verified to wake a running session, observed 2026-09-02T10:12Z. The genuine unknown is whether an Actions runner can fire one -- it holds no mcp__* tools -- and the watch_url alternative has two limits that shape the design rather than decorate it: the watch dies with the session, and THIS REPO IS PUBLIC so a webhook URL committed to it is a published endpoint. Design constraints that hold whichever transport wins: record the asking session (smallest change, gates everything); the push must CARRY the answer because a fired turn cannot go fetch it; one-way, so nothing waits for an ack; three states never collapsed (pushed / session_gone / unknown); and PUSH ADDS TO PULL rather than replacing it.
items.the_honest_residual: session_gone is not an edge case -- a long question is exactly the kind whose asking session dies before the answer lands, so the fallback is the common path and the push is the optimisation. A push-only design would silently lose answers precisely when they matter most. And a green test proves nothing here: the done-condition is an OBSERVED wake -- a session idle before and running after, doing something attributable to the push.
items.note: || OPERATOR DECISION 2026-09-02, dispatched to the session and recorded here because a decision that lives only in a transcript is the failure this build exists to end. THE 30-DAY CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN IS RULED OUT -- operator verbatim: 'we definitely can't have a flow that relies on my minting new tokens every month - but we also need to the 2 way flow here.' The REQUIREMENT STANDS; only that mechanism is dead, and the objection is to a human re-minting anything on a schedule, so a longer-lived token or a PAT is the same answer and is also ruled out. APPROVED SHAPE: C as the design (a blocking question ENDS the session and a fresh one is re-fired when the answer lands, so nothing must reach into a live session and nothing needs a credential to do it) - B as the mechanism (a standing cron Routine, fresh session per fire, hourly, draining committed decisions off /api/bot/work/decisions) - A as the fast path (session-bound Routine wake, PROVEN, used four times today). [!] C IS RIGHT AND NOT YET EARNED: it depends on the work object being resumable, which is Phase E, whose exit condition is 'killing a session mid-work loses nothing, DEMONSTRATED by killing one' and nobody has killed one. B is therefore the floor. [!] B IS THE SHAPE THAT HAS GONE INERT TWICE ON THIS ACCOUNT (Health Check Routine and Sprint Continue Work: enabled true, next_run_at 0001-01-01, never fired, still naming the pre-July repo name), so B IS NOT DONE WHEN THE ROUTINE EXISTS -- it is done when something WATCHES that it fired, via list_triggers.last_run. RULED OUT ON MEASUREMENT, not inference: watch_url mints a per-session inbound webhook at api.anthropic.com with no standing secret -- exactly the right shape -- and an unsigned POST returns 401; its sealed_secret is encrypted to the artifact service, so no GitHub workflow can ever sign a delivery. Probe created, POSTed, 401, unwatched.

items.tier: 1 (investigation); any fix depends on what it touches
items.observed: POPULATION: all 17 `automation/*` branches on origin (git ls-remote --heads), each tested with `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> origin/main`. RESULT: 0 landed, 17 unreachable. Span 2026-06-23 to 2026-09-02: 8 ciwatch-pr10757 result branches (today 06:00-07:20), work-digest (today 07:10), probes (today 09:44), econ-calendar (2026-08-29, which DOES have an open PR #10398), 2 research-queue stamps (2026-08-30), valuation-snapshots (2026-07-23), and 3 grade-order-packages carrying 1049 + 18 + 6 order-package decision grades (2026-06-23). Found while checking whether work-digest.yml had ever fired on cron for Phase B -- it HAS, twice: run #1 SUCCESS (00:19:37Z), run #2 FAILURE (07:10:05Z) which nobody had looked at four hours later.
items.what_complying_would_have_done: Nothing available would have caught it. The gap is that no check compares automation output against main. `claude-run-failure-alert` covers run failures, and whether it fired here is unestablished -- that is part of MI-62's brief and must be answered with a POSITIVE CONTROL, since 'it did not fire' and 'we could not show it can fire' are different findings.
items.root_cause: TWO CONFIRMED for today, the rest UNKNOWN and deliberately not generalised. CONFIRMED: work-digest run 33602234950 and work-decision-commit run 33618689721 each committed and pushed SUCCESSFULLY, then died at `gh pr create` on `GraphQL: API rate limit already exceeded for user ID 119055177` -- so the work exists on a branch and no PR was ever opened. The manager opened the second by hand (#10785, merged); the first is still stranded. NOT THE SAME CAUSE: #10398 has an OPEN PR, so its failure is a non-completing auto-merge; and the June/July branches predate today entirely. Asserting one cause for all 17 would be the unstated-population error this repo keeps paying for.
items.what_actually_prevents_it: MI-62, and its first job is a DISPOSITION PER BRANCH -- `superseded` (the content is on main by another route) / `lost` (it is not, and nothing regenerates it) / `unknown` (could not establish) -- checked against CONTENT, never the branch name. A stranded valuation snapshot may have been regenerated the next day; the 1049 grades may already be in comms/claude_strategy_scores.jsonl. The deeper deliverable is that a landing failure becomes VISIBLE: a retry on rate limit is a plaster, and the property that failed is Phase E's declared 'no work is lost'.
items.the_honest_residual: ⚠️ THIS BEARS ON A DECISION THE MANAGER ALREADY MADE. `.github/actions/commit-to-main` was approved this morning as the landing route for MI-57's post-merge reconciler (#10783) -- BEFORE this measurement existed. If that route strands work on a rate limit, the reconciler inherits it, and a reconciler that silently fails to land is WORSE than none because the record would then read as maintained while going stale. MI-62 must report on that specifically; it may reverse the approval. Also: the manager must not mass-merge or delete these branches to tidy up -- an unreachable branch is the only surviving copy of its work, and several are months old and may conflict or be wrong to re-land now.

items.title: Operator cap: at most 3 concurrent work sessions, scale up only on measured feasibility
items.observed: OPERATOR DIRECTIVE 2026-09-02, verbatim: 'I think we need to limit ourselves to 3 concuurent work sessions - 8 seems like too much for to handle reliably, so lets start small and scale up based on what we actually know is feasible', followed by 'LEt all the opne sessions close, but don't spawn new ones until 1 of the 3 slots is open'. So: no forced stand-downs, a spawn gate, and the number is provisional pending evidence.
items.what_complying_would_have_done: Nothing was violated -- this is a new constraint. What it corrects is a manager habit: this session spawned freely because the declared ceiling was 8, and the binding constraint was never the ceiling. It is the OPERATOR'S capacity to follow what is in flight, which no register measured.
items.root_cause: THE CAP IN THE DESIGN COUNTS A DIFFERENT THING FROM WHAT THE OPERATOR CAPPED, and conflating them would silently break CI. The operating model's WIP ceiling of 8 counts in_flight WORK OBJECTS (docs/claude/work/objects/*.yaml) and is enforced by scripts/ci/check_wip_ceiling.py. The operator capped concurrent WORK SESSIONS. These are different registers with different populations: measured 2026-09-02 there are 4 in_flight objects and 2 RUNNING sessions. Lowering the OBJECT ceiling to 3 would fail CI immediately on the 4 in_flight phase objects, which is not what was asked and would block the build. The session cap is therefore applied to SESSIONS, and the object ceiling is left at 8 pending an explicit operator call.
items.what_actually_prevents_it: The manager does not spawn while the count is at or above 3. [!] THE COUNT IS ASSIGNED-AND-UNFINISHED WORK, NOT `SESSION_STATUS_RUNNING`. An idle session that still owes a PR is a thing the operator is tracking, and counting only RUNNING would have read 2 today while four sessions held open work -- the permissive reading, and the one that reproduces the condition the cap exists to end. [!] AND A list_sessions PAGE IS NOT A POPULATION: the read that established today's number returned 40 rows with has_more true, so a count taken from one page must say so.
items.the_honest_residual: NOTHING ENFORCES THIS YET -- it is a manager discipline, and the register that would make it checkable (SESSIONS.json) is the same one measured INCOMPLETE twice: MI-15 found 3 of 6 absent, and a later census found 26 of 55 sessions unregistered with 17 carrying this manager's own id as parent. So a cap counted over that register would under-count exactly when it matters. Making it enforceable is real work and is not done here. [!] THE NUMBER IS PROVISIONAL BY THE OPERATOR'S OWN WORDING -- 'scale up based on what we actually know is feasible' -- so raising it needs evidence about handling capacity, not a busy week.

items.title: Claimed TELEGRAM_CLAUDE_BOT_SECRET was unset from a doc row, over the operator's own contrary observation
items.observed: Operator, 2026-09-02: 'I really can't believe we're going back to this again, we already established that the channel works!!!! JUST WIRE THE PR TO RIGHT BOT!!!' They were right. The manager told them TWICE that TELEGRAM_CLAUDE_BOT_SECRET was unset, and gated the ClaudeBot work on it, having never measured it. The claim came from OI-20260901-CLAUDE-CHANNEL-SEPARATION-SHIPPED-BUT-UNPROVEN (dated the PREVIOUS day) and from #10789's body saying its author could not read the VM. Neither is a measurement.
items.root_cause: FIELD BEATS COMMENT, INVERTED. The operator had ALREADY shown a ping arriving on ClaudeBot earlier the same day and said 'got this'. That is a direct observation of the channel working, and it was weighed BELOW a dated doc row. This repo's first rule is that a doc is a CLAIM about the field and the field wins; an operator's own sighting is field evidence, not opinion.
items.what_actually_prevents_it: The blocker was asserted, not measured, so it was never a blocker to remove -- it was a claim to check. The correct action is the one the operator gave: wire and merge, and let the DEPLOY be the measurement. The new unit exits EX_CONFIG into a visible `failed` state if the var really is missing, so one deploy settles it at less cost than two rounds of argument.
items.the_honest_residual: IT IS STILL NOT MEASURED. get-env's ALLOWED_KEYS admits a key only when its VALUE is safe to publish, so a bot token is not readable that way, and presence-vs-value is a distinction that path does not expose. The honest state is UNMEASURED -- not 'set', and not 'unset'. Do not close this row on the argument being over; close it on the deploy.

items.title: No manager handoff until the requisite flows are built, implemented AND verified working
items.observed: Operator-directed 2026-09-02: "I don't want to handoff before we are at least 200% certain that the requisite flows and merchanisms are built, implmented, and verified working correctly". Also, earlier the same hour: "i don't want to hand off before we're ready - that's why I keep asking you instead of telling you." So handoff readiness is the OPERATOR'S call and handoff_check's readiness=ready is NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT.
items.root_cause: handoff_check grades whether a SUCCESSOR CAN SEE the state -- registry, lease, checklist, open-PR rows. It says nothing about whether the MECHANISMS WORK. Those are different questions and this repo's whole vocabulary exists to keep them apart: landed_unproven is not done, a merge is not a deploy, and a deploy is not an observation.
items.what_actually_prevents_it: THE BAR, STATED AS OBSERVATIONS SO IT IS CHECKABLE RATHER THAN A FEELING. Each names what would settle it, and a green test settles NONE of them: (1) DECISION ROUND-TRIP ON CLAUDEBOT -- a tap on ClaudeBot producing a work_decision_transit row, then that same request grading `committed` on /api/bot/work/decisions with the answer block on main. Already PROVEN on the TRADER bot (10:11:42Z prompt, 10:16:36Z tap, submitted_by telegram); the ClaudeBot leg is not. [!] CORRECTED 2026-09-02 BY MI-58, AND THE MANAGER'S PREMISE WAS FALSE. The manager told MI-58 that 'once TELEGRAM_CLAUDE_BOT_SECRET is set, the fallback can never fire' and used that to argue for KEEPING the trader-bot fallback rather than making it fail-closed. WRONG: answerable_route() requires a live HEARTBEAT, not merely a token, so if ict-claude-decision-bot.service dies or is masked, decisions land on the trader bot again WITH THE SECRET SET. The fallback is PERMANENT, not a pre-secret window. The decision to keep it may still be right on its own merits -- a wrong chat is a noise complaint, holding every prompt is an outage -- but the reason given for it was not. [!] SO SETTING THE SECRET IS NOT THE POST-DEPLOY CHECK. Read /api/diag/log_file?name=telegram_poll_claude and `destination` in the sweep stats. 'Decisions still arrive' is NOT evidence the move happened -- that is precisely what the fallback produces. (2) /status AND /decisions -- the operator types each and gets a correct reply, ON CLAUDEBOT. #10793 is held as a draft precisely so this cannot be satisfied on the wrong bot. (3) PUSH-BACK TO THE ASKING SESSION (MI-60, #10788) -- a committed decision reaching the session that asked, without a minted token. B is not done when the Routine EXISTS; it is done when something WATCHES that it FIRED (list_triggers.last_run), because two Routines on this account were enabled and never once fired. (4) THE WORK STORE -- a COLD session, not pointed there by its prompt, acting on the readout or the cycle priority and citing where it read it. (5) NO WORK IS LOST (Phase E) -- demonstrated BY KILLING A SESSION MID-WORK, not asserted from a test. Nobody has killed one. (6) THE DAILY DIGEST -- one run with event=schedule. A workflow_dispatch run is not a cron run.
items.the_honest_residual: [!] THE MANAGER IS THE WRONG JUDGE OF (4) AND CANNOT CLEAR IT. A cold observation is by definition made by a session that was not told, and this manager built or dispatched most of these. Record WHICH session made each observation. [!] AND DO NOT LET THIS ROW BECOME A REASON NEVER TO HAND OFF. It is a bar, not a veto: if a mechanism turns out to be unverifiable rather than merely unverified, that is a finding to report to the operator, not a condition to wait out forever.

items.title: The most privileged role in the system has no skill, so every manager re-derives the job from prose and repeats the same mistakes
items.spawn_when: After MI-66, or in the same session if scope allows. Both are enactment of the operating-layer inventory.
items.observed: Operator, 2026-09-02: 'how do we ensure that you future manager session don't make the same mistake?' MEASURED in answering it: 32 skills exist and NOT ONE is a manager role pack. The role that merges, deploys, spawns sessions, holds the lease and answers to the operator is the only significant role with no pack. Everything a manager knows arrives as prose -- CLAUDE.md, a sweep-trigger prompt, and whatever the previous manager wrote in a checklist note.
items.root_cause: DOCUMENTATION HAS ALREADY BEEN TRIED AND MEASURABLY FAILED, and that is the whole argument for this row. The CI-never-fired trap is stated VERBATIM in CLAUDE.md ('if such a commit lands last your PR shows ZERO checks and is blocked, not green -- push an ordinary commit after, to arm CI'). The manager session of 2026-09-02 had read that line and hit the trap THREE TIMES the same afternoon (#10793, #10795, #10789). Restating a rule that is known and still broken is not a fix; this repo's own F4 says a repeated mistake becomes an executable check or it is not a lesson.
items.scope: A `manager` skill carrying (a) the loop -- lease heartbeat, read the registers, merge one at a time re-verifying between, review before un-drafting, spawn through the registry -- and (b) an EXECUTABLE PREFLIGHT rather than a list of reminders. The preflight must include, at minimum, the four failures measured on 2026-09-02: 1. BEFORE trusting `total_count: 0`, read mergeable_state AND the head commit's AUTHOR -- a bot-authored head means CI never fired (BL-20260902-BOARD-POST-RELAY-SILENTLY-KILLS-CI-ON-THE-PR-OF-ANY-SESSION-THAT-FOLLOWS-THE-PROTOCOL...). 2. BEFORE landing a register-touching manager PR, check what sibling PRs it will re-conflict; the manager is the highest-frequency writer to those files (BL-20260902-FIVE-MONOLITHIC-JSON-REGISTERS-RECONFLICT-EVERY-SIBLING-PR-ON-EVERY-MERGE...). 3. BEFORE blocking work on a claim about live state, PROBE it. The 2026-09-02 manager blocked the ClaudeBot work on 'TELEGRAM_CLAUDE_BOT_SECRET is unset', asserted from a doc row dated the previous day, against the operator's own contrary sighting (MI-65). 4. BEFORE a read-append-write on any register, confirm the file round-trips; OPEN-ITEMS.json does not (BL-20260902-OPEN-ITEMS-IS-THE-ONE-REGISTER-NO-APPEND-HELPER-PROTECTS). 5. F6 -- REFUSE TO PROCEED when the count of unnotified autonomous actions since the last ping exceeds a stated threshold. This is the fifth item and arguably the first in importance: F6 is the CONDITION the autonomy grant rests on, and on 2026-09-02 a manager merged 5 PRs, dispatched 4 sessions, held a PR to block a deploy and made a fallback design call across ~8 hours while sending ZERO pings -- the operator noticed before the manager did. The class of action most worth reporting is exactly the class that is silent, because merge_pull_request / update_pull_request / create_session / fire_trigger are MCP calls with no notification hop, while the narrow VM system-actions DO carry one. BL-20260902-THE-MANAGERS-HIGH-IMPACT-ACTIONS-BYPASS-EVERY-PATH-THAT-NOTIFIES.
items.what_actually_prevents_it: An executable preflight the manager RUNS, not a section it reads -- the `handoff_check.py` shape, which already refuses `ready` rather than grading a soft pass, and which is the one manager mechanism that has worked reliably today. Every item above is checkable from a script.
items.the_honest_residual: [!] A SKILL IS STILL PROSE UNTIL THE CHECKS EXIST. Writing a `manager` SKILL.md and stopping there would reproduce exactly the failure this row documents -- and would be harder to see, because the role pack would LOOK like the fix. The deliverable is the checks; the skill is where they are invoked from. [!] AND IT INHERITS MI-66's FINDING: no role pack references the operating layer at all, so a new manager pack must point at the work store, the readout and the caps rather than the pre-2026-09-01 world of three backlogs and DUE.md. Writing it against the old world would add a 33rd skill with the same gap.
items.landed_unproven_because: #10808 MERGED 2026-09-02 (67cfb8be). ⚠️ TWO OF THE THREE MECHANISMS WORK AND THE THIRD CANNOT. The manager VERIFIED spawn_gate.py on both controls itself -- out-of-priority exits 3, in-priority exits 0. But queue_latency.py grades `unknown` PERMANENTLY: its verdict needs a live list_sessions read and CI holds no mcp__* tools. Honest, and not yet a guard. MI-73 owns closing that.

items.title: A rebase or merge of main arms auto-merge on a claude/** branch, because the push diff includes everything main changed
items.observed: Found and filed by MI-58. claude-pr-automerge.yml still carries the LEGACY shared marker `.github/pr-automerge-request` in its paths: filter and that file is still in the tree, so any claude/** branch that merges or rebases main touches the path and is UN-DRAFTED AND ARMED having asked for nothing. [!] THIS EXPLAINS AN OBSERVATION THE MANAGER MADE AND COULD NOT ACCOUNT FOR: on #10795 the manager noted that github-actions[bot] un-drafted the PR and enabled auto-merge 'without a marker file in my diff' and flagged it as odd. This is the cause. The manager had the symptom; MI-58 had the mechanism.
items.what_actually_prevents_it: Remove the legacy shared path from the workflow's paths: filter so ONLY the per-request .github/pr-automerge-requests/<slug>.txt opt-in arms it. That per-request path is already the documented convention and its README records why the shared marker was wrong.
items.the_honest_residual: [!] DELETING A HOLD FILE IS NOT THE FIX. A test-file hold WAS deleted on 2026-09-02 (correctly, for an unrelated reason) and could be mistaken for remediation. The mechanism is untouched.
items.note: #10810 reviewed by the manager and ARMED 2026-09-02, not yet merged. Its central finding is that removing the legacy shared marker FIXES NOTHING ON ITS OWN -- measured across the three misfires, that path appears in ZERO of them; what matched is the GLOB, because any branch merging main drags other branches' request files into its push diff. The real fix is a REQUEST GATE proving THIS branch asked, plus never un-drafting a PR the workflow did not create.

items.title: Decision PRESENTATION on ClaudeBot: options as a readable list, and real multiple choice
items.tier: 2 (touches the Telegram bridge; no order path, no strategy config, no risk caps)
items.raised_by: operator, 2026-09-02, in conversation, EXPLICITLY not urgent: 'Also not urgent, but something that I do want us to have ... somewhere in our work plan.'
items.observed: Operator, on the live decision prompt: 'the point with the buttons is that it's very shortened, a little cut off ... maybe there's more of a list and I can click the options, maybe some would be multiple choice. I think that button is a good first step, but probably not the end of where this design needs to go.' So the ASK half of the decision round-trip works and its PRESENTATION is the limit.
items.⚠️_the_truncation_is_the_LABEL_not_the_c: DO NOT go looking for a callback_data size bug -- it is already solved and re-solving it would waste the session. `callback_data` is 26 bytes FIXED (`wdec:<12 hex>:<8 hex>`) against Telegram's 64-byte cap, and it carries a DIGEST of the option KEY, deliberately never a positional index. What the operator sees cut off is the BUTTON LABEL, which Telegram renders narrow and elides. Those are different layers.

the_shape_to_build.1_options_as_a_numbered_list_in_the_MESS: Put the full option text in the message body as a numbered list -- where there is room for it -- and reduce each button to its number. The body is not width-constrained the way a button is, so the option a person is choosing between becomes readable without touching the callback contract at all. This is the cheap half and it is probably most of the win.
the_shape_to_build.2_multiple_choice_is_NOT_one_press: [!] A single inline keyboard press submits ONE value, so multi-select is not a formatting change -- it needs a TOGGLE keyboard: each tap flips an option's mark and re-renders the keyboard, and an explicit Submit sends the set. That means holding PARTIAL, UNSUBMITTED state between taps, which the current design deliberately does not have. Decide where that state lives BEFORE building it; a half-submitted answer that looks submitted is the forward-failure the transit contract exists to refuse.
the_shape_to_build.3_free_text_is_still_a_separate_step: Unchanged and deliberately not half-built: inline buttons cannot carry arbitrary text. A request declaring no options is still SENT (so a blocking question is never invisible) and says plainly that it needs an answer on the SPA or in the repo.

items.what_must_not_regress: The four never-collapsed answer states (`not_submitted`/`in_transit`/`committed`/`unreadable`); the option token staying a KEY DIGEST rather than an index (an index silently records a different answer if the object is reordered between send and tap); the fail-closed write gate; and the confirmation continuing to read 'Submitted -- NOT yet decided'.
items.why_deferred: P1 is the handoff capability and P2 is the overhaul implementation. This is a UX improvement to a channel that already works end-to-end -- the round-trip was observed complete on 2026-09-02. The operator said not urgent and this records that as a decision, not as an oversight.

items.title: The daily manager cadence: day session → declared wrap → night manager → morning brief
items.raised_by: operator, 2026-09-02, in conversation, as the shape the handoff should take
items.⚠️_THIS_SUPERSEDES_THE_MANAGERS_OWN_FRAM: The manager reported that `open_prs` completeness is POINT-IN-TIME and concluded 'a handoff has to be taken in a QUIET WINDOW, or the check needs a bounded tolerance.' That framing is PASSIVE -- it waits for a quiet moment that a busy repo never reliably offers. The operator's answer is ACTIVE and is better: you do not wait for a quiet window, you CREATE one, by declaring per thread which PR is the LAST one before the manager moves on. Do not re-derive the tolerance idea from the old framing; the boundary is declared, not awaited.

the_cycle.1_morning: The day STARTS WITH A PING — a daily brief into a NEW manager session. ⚠️ The brief must carry WHAT WAS DONE OVERNIGHT and what was wrapped up after the operator went to bed. Operator: 'by the [brief] in the morning, I want that to include what was done overnight and what was wrapped up after I went to bed, so that I know where I'm starting off from.' A brief that only describes the new day's plan fails its purpose.
the_cycle.3_wrap: The operator SAYS when they are going to bed. That is the trigger, not a clock. The manager then produces a RAPID WRAP PLAN: (a) the LAST PR for each thread; (b) confirmation that NO Tier-3 decision is left dangling -- and any that is gets LOGGED FOR THE NEXT DAY rather than carried in a session's head; (c) close everything down.
the_cycle.4_night: The manager SETS OFF THE NIGHT SESSION ITSELF, scoped by HOW MUCH TIME IT HAS until the morning brief. Night work is deliberately the low-operator-dependency kind: backlog items and UI, 'things that are less important and need less of me, and very easy to run without me.' ⚠️ NOTHING TIER-3 AND NOTHING NEEDING A DECISION goes to the night session -- it cannot get an answer.

items.the_last_PR_per_thread_rule: ⚠️ READ WHAT THE OPERATOR RULED OUT, not just what they asked for. They explicitly did NOT ask that entire MILESTONES be finished before a handoff: 'it just means that for each thread of workflow, we need to decide what the last PR for each manager is gonna be before we move on, and that needs to be documented clearly so that we can make sure that we're sticking to that.' So the unit is a DECLARED TERMINAL PR PER THREAD, documented in advance and held to -- not milestone completion, which would block every handoff indefinitely.
items.what_this_needs_built: Not yet designed, and deliberately not designed here: where the per-thread terminal PR is DECLARED (OPEN-PRS.json rows already carry a thread via checklist_item, so this may be a field rather than a new register); how the morning brief is GENERATED from the overnight record rather than written by hand; and whether the night session's scope is bounded by a stated deadline it can read. Operator also raised timers/pings for start-and-finish awareness -- worth a design pass, not a guess.
items.⚠️_honest_precondition: The operator's own read: 'it sounds like we still have a lot of [work] here to get [addressed] so that we're able to do an actual reliable handoff.' This item does NOT claim the cadence is achievable today. handoff_check.py still reads not_ready more often than ready on a busy repo.
items.⚠️_CORRECTION_THE_MANAGER_MADE_TO_ITSELF: THE NIGHT HOP NEEDS NO NEW MECHANISM, and the first version of this row said it did. It read: 'the night-manager hop depends on a fresh-session-per-fire routine gated on the lease, which does not exist.' That is FALSE for the flow the operator actually described, which has the MANAGER setting the night session off directly -- 'set off the night manager session yourself' -- and `create_session` is proven to do exactly that (MI-73 was spawned with it on 2026-09-02). Overstating a blocker is not a safe error: it invites a session to build a routine nobody needs and to treat tonight's handoff as impossible when it is not.
items.what_ACTUALLY_needs_a_mechanism: ⚠️ DECIDED 2026-09-02 — THE MORNING WAKE IS MANUAL, AND THIS IS AN ANSWER, NOT A GAP. Operator, verbatim: 'There's [no] new need for a timer or a trigger for the morning manager. I will do that manually. I will get the daily brief. I will read it, and then I will use it as the beginning of a prompt, which I'll also add my notes to, to set off the manager session for that day. So that doesn't need to be set off automatically. I wanna be there at the beginning.' So: NO cron routine, NO create_new_session_on_fire, NO lease-gated auto-spawn. Do not build one, and do not re-open this as an oversight -- the operator being present at the start of the day is a DELIBERATE choice, and automating it would remove the point.
items.⚠️_the_self_bound_sweep_limit_is_still_r: Unchanged by the correction above: the manager sweep re-armed 2026-09-02T15:20Z is SELF-BOUND and dies with its session. That is a genuine gap for a manager that DIES mid-day -- it is simply not the gap the night handoff has, because the night handoff is deliberate and the manager is alive to perform it.
items.⚠️_what_the_manual_wake_does_NOT_remove: THE BRIEF ITSELF IS STILL A DELIVERABLE AND IS STILL UNBUILT. The operator says 'I will GET the daily brief' -- they are the trigger, not the author. Something must PRODUCE a brief that carries what happened overnight, and that is precisely the half their stated reason depends on: 'so that I know where I'm starting off from.' Separating these two matters, because the wake being settled makes it easy to read the whole morning end as settled. The wake is decided; the brief is open. Most likely the NIGHT session's closing output is the brief, which would make it a night-session deliverable rather than a new mechanism -- but that is a proposal, not a decision, and nobody has built it.

items.title: A notifications menu per bot: choose WHICH notifications, and a CADENCE for the periodic ones
items.tier: 2 (Telegram bridge + a stored per-chat preference; no order path, no strategy config, no risk caps)
items.raised_by: operator, 2026-09-02, in conversation, EXPLICITLY for the backlog: 'a further idea, though, that I do want us to backlog as well ... so that we eventually get to it.'
items.observed: Operator: 'in the menu for each of the bots for there to be an option for notifications, which would then pull up a list of the notifications, and I could choose which ones. And for the ones that are periodic, there should be some choices for cadence -- hourly, daily, weekly, maybe once, twice, three times daily, depending on what kind of thing it is.' Raised alongside making the work digest hourly, which is the manual version of exactly this control.
items.⚠️_HALF_OF_THIS_ALREADY_EXISTS_AND_LOST_: DO NOT BUILD THE 'WHICH' HALF FROM SCRATCH -- measure it first. A per-kind subscription model is already shipped and has been since M12: `GET /api/bot/devices/event-kinds` serves the canonical taxonomy from `src.runtime.mobile_push.event_kinds` (kind/label/description/in_flight) precisely so a client need not mirror the list, and `PATCH /api/bot/devices/{id}/subscriptions` stores a per-device choice as `null|[kinds]|{kind:bool}`. It was built for the Android app's Notifications screen -- and the Android app was RETIRED from the live feed on 2026-09-01, with `device_tokens` measured EMPTY (0 registered devices). So this is a mechanism that is written, works, and now has no reader: the `provenance-consumer-guard` shape one level up, the same shape MI-70 found with the `Claude-Session:` commit trailer. The honest framing of this item is RE-POINT AN EXISTING TAXONOMY AT TELEGRAM, plus build the genuinely new half.

what_is_genuinely_new.cadence_per_kind: The existing model is a BOOLEAN per kind (on/off). Cadence is a third value and the taxonomy has no field for it. Note the operator's own distinction -- 'depending on what kind of thing it is' -- so cadence is not universal: an EVENT (a decision ready, an incident) is immediate-or-nothing and a cadence choice on it is meaningless, while a DIGEST (the work digest, the daily roll-up) is exactly where cadence belongs. The taxonomy therefore needs to say which kinds are cadence-BEARING, or the menu will offer 'weekly' on an alert.
what_is_genuinely_new.per_CHAT_not_per_DEVICE: `device_tokens` is keyed on an FCM token. Telegram has no such token; the natural key is the chat/bot pair. Whether that is a new table or a widened one is the first design question, and it is the one that decides how much of the existing model is reusable.
what_is_genuinely_new.a_menu_is_stateful: Same constraint as MI-71: one inline press submits one value, so a multi-select preferences screen is a TOGGLE keyboard plus an explicit Save, which means holding partial unsubmitted state. The two items share this problem and should probably share its solution -- do not solve it twice, differently.

items.⚠️_what_must_not_become_switchable: A preferences menu that can silence anything is a way to turn off an alarm and forget. The severity-band rule stands: a P0 (money at risk) page is NOT a preference. Whatever this ships with, the CRITICAL/unprotected-position class must remain unmutable, or this feature becomes the desensitized-alarm P1 with a UI in front of it.
items.why_deferred: P1 is the handoff capability, P2 the overhaul implementation. The operator asked for it to be backlogged, not built, and the immediate need it came with -- an hourly work digest -- was satisfied directly by a cron change.

items.title: The manager watcher is BLIND by construction — give it a sensor that can actually see
items.observed: Of the three mechanisms MI-68 built to watch the manager (merged #10808), TWO WORK and the third cannot. `spawn_gate.py` was verified by the manager on BOTH controls -- out-of-priority object exits 3, in-priority exits 0. But `queue_latency.py`, the one aimed at the manager sitting on a blocked queue, reports `unknown` PERMANENTLY: its verdict needs a live `list_sessions` read, that is an mcp__* tool, and CI holds no MCP tools. It refuses to substitute SESSIONS.json's stale `last_observed`, which is correct -- that register has been measured incomplete twice.
items.why_it_matters: This is the failure that cost the most on 2026-09-02: four sub-sessions sat IDLE and BLOCKED on the manager for up to 142 minutes while the manager asserted they held work. It is also the operator's core ask -- 'actual guards and mechanisms in the repo/vm themselves that watch the manager and enforce the rules on him.' A permanently-`unknown` watcher is honest but is not yet that guard.
items.the_hypothesis_to_TEST_not_assume: The same failure has an MCP-FREE PROXY that GitHub Actions can see with nothing but its own GITHUB_TOKEN: a PR green/mergeable/unmerged and ageing; a `needs_action` posted with nothing since; a board `▶️ START` with no `✅ DONE`, ageing; an `in_flight` checklist item whose owner's branch has had no push for N hours. ⚠️ THE MANAGER BELIEVES THIS AND HAS NOT PROVEN IT. If the proxy is weaker than it looks, a STATED BOUNDARY is the better deliverable -- which is exactly what MI-68 delivered on queue_latency and why its work merged.
items.what_must_not_regress: (a) Do NOT delete or weaken the `unknown` path -- `quiet`/`escalate`/`unknown` must never collapse, because 'we could not look' and 'nothing is waiting' are opposite facts. (b) It must NOT be invokable by the manager: MI-68's own measurement is that every mechanism the manager had to choose to run went unused, and every mechanism that stood in the way worked. (c) Never page on activity, only on a state that is actually stuck, rate-limited per class -- 202 of 376 CRITICAL rows in one measured window here were a single un-latched alarm.
items.⚠️_a_cron_is_not_evidence_of_a_run: work-digest.yml's own header records a scheduled workflow in this repo firing ~4h50m LATE and once instead of daily. Whatever carries this must make its own liveness checkable.
items.⚠️_outcome: DIED BLOCKED, WORK LOST. post_turn_summary: 'blocked on permission classifier; auto-mode denied add_repo x2 and git push x3'. It never pushed a branch, so ~$10 of work is unrecoverable -- exactly the loss MI-70 demonstrated by killing a session. Two manager wake attempts did not clear it: the denial is its session's permission classifier, which the manager cannot change from outside. SUPERSEDED BY MI-77, respawned with an explicit source_url (which this session's context lacked) and instructed to push within its first minutes. [!] THE MANAGER'S FIRST DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG AND IS RECORDED AS SUCH: it told MI-73 the cause was an omitted source_url, then found MI-75 had a source it never passed and MI-76 acquired one late -- sources attach ASYNCHRONOUSLY, so 'no sources' reads as a defect when it is often just a timing artifact.

items.title: Phase E: prove no work is lost by actually killing a session mid-work
items.landed_unproven_because: #10812 and #10820 both MERGED 2026-09-02. ⚠️ THE REAPER HAS STILL NEVER BEEN OBSERVED RUNNING TO COMPLETION, and #10820 is why that matters: the version merged in #10812 pushed straight to PROTECTED main (GH006), so every scheduled run would have reaped correctly and RECORDED NOTHING -- a frozen ledger reading exactly like a quiet week. The owner found that itself, after merge, and fixed it via .github/actions/commit-to-main with verify-merged: true.
items.the_ruling_it_carries: ⚠️ PHASE E DOES NOT CLOSE ON THIS. The kill was RUN and demonstrated a PARTIAL loss -- 'killing a session loses everything it had not pushed, and nothing it had' -- which CONTRADICTS the object's done-condition ('loses nothing'). Manager ruled 2026-09-02: do NOT amend the condition to match the result (that fits the bar to the outcome) and do NOT leave 'loses nothing' standing (unachievable -- the loss is in a dead container no reaper can reach). BOUND it instead, and keep Phase E open until a successor object exists for PUSH CADENCE, which is the only lever that moves the number.
items.⚠️_do_not_merge: `claude/mi70-kill-subject` must NEVER be merged. It is the EVIDENCE for the kill demonstration and holds a throwaway notes file.

items.title: The HANDOFF BRIEF — what a successor manager and the operator are handed, generated not written
items.why_this_is_the_last_P1_gap: The operator set the daily cadence and then decided BOTH hops are MANUAL -- the manager spawns the night session (create_session, proven), and the operator starts the morning one because 'I wanna be there at the beginning.' That CLOSED the wake question and left exactly one thing open: they say they will GET the daily brief. They are the TRIGGER, not the author, and NOTHING PRODUCES ONE.
items.acceptance_is_the_operators_own_words: 'by the [brief] in the morning, I want that to include what was done overnight and what was wrapped up after I went to bed, SO THAT I KNOW WHERE I'M STARTING OFF FROM.' A brief that renders but does not answer that fails, however well-formed it is.
items.two_consumers_and_it_is_an_open_question: (1) THE OPERATOR IN THE MORNING -- readable prose they paste as the opening of the next manager's prompt, carrying what happened overnight. (2) A SUCCESSOR MANAGER MID-DAY -- live state: checklist, in-flight sessions, open PRs with their operator decisions AND conditions, loud open-items, the lease, what is blocked and on what. The owner was told to ARGUE the choice rather than assume it.
items.⚠️_the_real_constraint_it_must_not_fake_: What MERGED is readable from git and the registers are readable, but WHAT A NIGHT SESSION CONCLUDED lives in get_session's post_turn_summary -- and mcp__* tools are unavailable to CI and to routine-fired turns. So the brief is probably a CLOSE-OUT DELIVERABLE the night manager runs before it ends, not a cron. The owner must decide that honestly and say which.
items.what_must_not_regress: GENERATED never hand-written (a hand-written brief dies with its session, which is the failure Phase E exists for); it must DECLARE what it could not read rather than silently omitting a register; and it must not flatten `landed_unproven` into `done` -- saying an item is finished when its effect was never observed actively misinforms the person starting the day.

items.title: The manager watcher that can actually see (MI-73 respawn)
items.why: Of MI-68's three manager-watching mechanisms, TWO WORK (spawn_gate verified by the manager on both controls) and queue_latency.py grades `unknown` PERMANENTLY because its verdict needs a live list_sessions read and CI holds no mcp__* tools. Honest, and not yet the guard the operator asked for.
items.the_hypothesis_to_TEST: An MCP-free proxy visible to Actions with only GITHUB_TOKEN: a green/mergeable/UNMERGED PR ageing; a needs_action with nothing since; a board START with no DONE; an in_flight item whose owner's branch has had no push for N hours. ⚠️ THE MANAGER BELIEVES THIS AND HAS NOT PROVEN IT -- a stated boundary is the better deliverable if the proxy is weaker than it looks.
items.what_must_not_regress: Do not collapse quiet/escalate/unknown. Must NOT be manager-invokable (every mechanism the manager had to choose to run went unused; every one that stood in the way worked). Never page on activity. And a cron is not evidence of a run -- session-reaper.yml had FIVE failing runs before its first success because it pushed to protected main, so this must land through .github/actions/commit-to-main with verify-merged: true.

items.title: Two open non-draft PRs are RED on pytest-run and nothing is driving them
items.why: #10764 (the CLAUDE.md instruction-surface split, MI-41-B) and #10810 (the automerge request gate, MI-69) are both non-draft, both mergeable, and both RED on pytest-run since 16:43Z, with their sub-sessions ended. Two finished operating-layer deliverables sitting undeliverable with no owner.

items.the_hypothesis_to_TEST: NOT 'move it to a Routine' -- that is the manager's hypothesis and MI-80 is deliberately told not to inherit it. Three candidates to rule in or out with evidence: (a) GitHub deprioritises scheduled workflows on a busy repo; (b) the job's own shape -- budget 40 minutes because commit-to-main waits up to 30m for its auto-merge PR, with concurrency cancel-in-progress:false, so an hourly cadence and a 40-minute job OVERLAP BY DESIGN and that may be the whole story; (c) the right fix is not a new carrier at all but that a MISSED SLOT BECOMES VISIBLE -- today a missed digest and a quiet hour are indistinguishable. Contrast worth testing against: Claude Routines on the same account fire on time (the :26 sweep fired 54s late) while GitHub cron is hours off or absent.
items.done_when: The digest arrives on a cadence OBSERVED over at least 6 consecutive expected slots with the misses COUNTED rather than assumed, and a missed or FAILED run is itself surfaced. Moving the carrier is not sufficient on its own -- a new carrier must be measured against its declared slots the same way GitHub's was. A workflow_dispatch run is NOT evidence the cron works.

items.title: The overdue trainer row — observe it, and build the data-freshness alarm if one can be built
items.tier: 1 (trainer read; trainer VM is autonomous territory)
items.why: OI-20260829-TRAINER-IS-NOW-A-DECIDED-DEPENDENCY-AND-IS-UNMONITORED is FOUR days past a THREE-day cadence. The operator DECIDED on 2026-08-29 to keep the trainer for L2 order-flow capture -- a forward-only stream nothing can re-derive -- and the row records the disk at 92% with nothing watching. The row is loud and renders in the CLAUDE.md brief and was STILL not observed, which makes it a live instance of the failure OI-20260826-SESSION-BRIEF-NEVER-READ-BY-A-FRESH-SESSION watches: the register surfaces it and nobody acts.
items.the_hypothesis_to_TEST: The two halves are DIFFERENT FACTS and must not be collapsed. (1) OBSERVE -- what is the disk headroom, is the capture still writing, how stale is its newest data. (2) ALARM -- keyed on the DATA's freshness at the named path, NEVER on the unit's ActiveState, because a systemd unit can be `active` while writing nothing and a unit-state alarm would be green straight through the failure this watches. The row's own clears_when requires the alarm be SHOWN to fire against PLANTED staleness, not merely deployed.
items.done_when: The row's observation carries what was SEEN (verbatim, with the command) and verified_at is re-dated. The row clears only if the freshness alarm exists AND was shown to fire against planted staleness; otherwise it stays open with the reason. Disk headroom recovering on its own does NOT clear it -- the gap is the missing alarm, not the free space.
items.note: DONE_WHEN MET on both halves, 2026-09-03 (MI-81). ⚠️ STATE WAS `landed_unproven` AND THAT IS NOW WRONG IN THE UNDERSTATING DIRECTION — `landed_unproven` means the effect has NOT been seen on the fleet, and it HAS been.
